summary.intent: Run the full post-execute-phase loop for Phase 66 (API schema cutover, publish gate, tombstone) autonomously: verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E → CodeRabbit CLI → ship → resolve PR reviews, without babysitting.
summary.outcome: PR #584 opened with 6 security/hardening fix commits on top of Phase 66's 55 commits. Both CI failures (coverage thresholds from deleted specs, SDK E2E Test 15 timing) were diagnosed and fixed with additional commits. All greptile review threads resolved; merge decision left to user.

repo: Phase 66 deleted all 5 shares spec files (shares.controller, share-invites.controller, invites.controller, share-invite.service, shares.service) without rewriting them, leaving the entire shares module at 0% coverage and failing CI coverage thresholds on the first push.
The CI Typecheck job (`pnpm typecheck`) only covers web + scripts, not apps/api specs; api specs are type-checked by ts-jest during the Test job (no isolatedModules — full type checking).

jest global coverageThreshold excludes files that have per-file thresholds, so covering shares.service.ts (0→92% branches) was sufficient to lift the global branch threshold above 78% even though controller branch coverage was lower.

The mock-ipns-routing delegated routing publish is fire-and-forget (no await for propagation), causing the at-floor serve in Test 15 to return null in slower CI environments while passing 3/3 locally.

Migration files can accumulate prettier formatting drift that bypasses local pre-commit hooks (automated GSD commits skip them) but fails the CI `eslint .` step — the pre-commit hook is not enforced on automated commits.

api:generate only produces formatting churn (single-line → multi-line array) for validation-only DTO regex changes; semantically the openapi.json is identical and should be reverted to avoid noise commits.
GSD enforcement hooks (secure-phase, validate-phase) are disabled in project config — the workflow gates must be run manually even though the ship-phase process requires them.

The `share_invites` claim path silently granted write authority from claimer DTO input (`dto.writeDescriptorRef`) without gating on whether the invite carried write authority (`invite.writeDescriptorRef`), a T-66-E1 presence-derived escalation the phase claimed to mitigate.

CodeRabbit CLI surfaced 15 findings on the committed diff, of which ~8 were false positives about `FolderIpns` (the entity was fully removed; the API built and booted successfully proving DI resolved).

The `tombstoneRecord` service method discarded the TypeORM `affected` count, returning HTTP 200 for non-existent, unowned, and already-tombstoned record names — greptile caught this independently of the security auditor.

code.finding: T-66-E1 bug: writeDescriptorRef was derived from dto.writeDescriptorRef without gating on invite.writeDescriptorRef, allowing a read-only invite claimer to supply an attacker-controlled write descriptor ref and obtain write authority.
Comment claimed 'Write grant is presence-derived from writeDescriptorRef (T-66-E1)' but the implementation below it did not implement the gate — the comment predated the bug fix.
New tombstone endpoint was missing @Throttle decorator while every sibling endpoint (publish, batch, unenroll, resolve) had it — oversight on a phase-new destructive endpoint.
rootIpnsName used loose /^k[a-z0-9]+$/ regex while sibling DTOs (resolve, tombstone) used the canonical k51qzi5uqu5.../bafzaa... strict validator — inconsistency introduced by the schema cutover.
Same loose /^k[a-z0-9]+$/ regex on rootIpnsName — tightened to canonical pattern alongside create-share.dto.
syncIpnsRecordSequence lacked a tombstonedAt IS NULL guard, so the republish race window could bump a tombstoned row's sequence — greptile P2.
Assertion on the update() criteria needed updating to include tombstonedAt: IsNull() after the guard was added to the service — one spec broke deterministically rather than being a flake.

Test 15 at-floor serve: delegated routing publish is fire-and-forget so in slow CI the resolve runs before propagation returns null. Fixed with a bounded poll (up to 6s) for eventual consistency — not a regression.

workflow: The commit helper can report commit_failed while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` before retrying, never blindly re-commit.
After `gh pr create`, the release bot pushes a chore(release) commit to the branch — `git fetch` + rebase is mandatory before every subsequent push or it will be rejected.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — always patch PR body via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
Greptile bundles findings in inline review threads; CodeRabbit re-reviews fix commits and can raise new findings on your own changes — always poll for re-reviews after pushing fixes.

Running `pnpm api:generate` to verify an openapi surface change is safe, but the command runs repo-wide `eslint .` which fails on pre-existing generated files (landing/.astro/types.d.ts) — check semantic diff and revert if cosmetic-only.

When a CI failure shows coverage-threshold violations (not test failures), the jest log output shows 'Jest: Global coverage threshold for branches (X%) not met' — look for this pattern, not just FAIL/PASS lines.

Adversarially verify subagent spec outputs: check the T-66-E1 assertion is real (toBeNull() would fail against pre-fix code), confirm no impl files were touched, and run the spec independently before committing.
A full `jest --coverage` run (854 tests) takes significant time but is the only authoritative gate; scoped per-file runs can pass individually while the global threshold still fails.
Prettier formatting errors in generated files (specs) committed by subagents will fail CI lint — always run `prettier --write` on subagent-authored files before committing.

friction: CodeRabbit CLI failed on first invocation with a service connection error, requiring a manual retry.
Greptile thread reply mutations hit network timeouts on the first attempt; resolves succeeded but reply content had to be re-posted for P1.

CI Lint failure on first push due to pre-existing prettier drift in the migration file (ApiSchemaCutover.ts) committed by an automated GSD commit that bypassed the pre-commit hook — required a separate cleanup commit.
CI Test and SDK E2E both failed after the first push, requiring diagnosis (coverage thresholds from deleted specs + Test 15 timing issue) and two additional fix commits, adding CI round-trips.
The full jest coverage run output was drowned by NestJS bootstrap logs, requiring a separate `--verbose=false` re-run to see the summary line.

The `api:generate` command runs repo-wide eslint which fails on `landing/.astro/types.d.ts` (pre-existing generated file) — a false blocker that had to be investigated before reverting the openapi churn.
The git commit after validate-phase timed out in the bash call even though both commits landed — required an extra verification step.
89 SDK E2E tests remain under `describe.skip` quarantine (D-01 milestone quarantine), making the suite results harder to interpret at a glance.
CodeRabbit emitted findings in batches as it streamed (3 → 9 → 15 findings), requiring multiple triage passes rather than a single complete list.
